links.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of four commercial ICH detection AI vendors on same local CT data
links.effect: AUROC 0.96-0.99 and sensitivity 0.85-0.92 with no significant pairwise differences; solutions B and D had significantly higher specificity (1.00, 0.99), precision (0.90-0.98) and F1 (0.87-0.94) than others (P<0.05).
links.quote: In binary performance, both solutions B and D exhibited significantly higher specificity (1.00 and 0.99), precision (0.90 to 0.98), and F1 score (0.87 to 0.94) than the other solutions (P < 0.05).

links.outcome: Side-by-side local comparison of candidate AI products to inform selection
links.effect: Meaningful differences emerged among four products in confirmatory performance and volumetric agreement despite similar AUROC; no single solution universally optimal.
links.quote: The algorithm-specific performance trade-offs identified in this study suggest that no single AI solution is universally optimal

links.outcome: Local performance of vendor AI against neuroradiologist reference standard on emergency CT data
links.effect: High AUROC (0.96-0.99) and sensitivity (0.85-0.92) locally across four solutions, but precision, specificity and volumetric agreement differed by vendor.
links.quote: However, meaningful differences emerged in confirmatory performance and volumetric agreement.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation and head-to-head comparison of diagnostic accuracy and volumetric agreement of four commercial AI solutions for intracranial hemorrhage detection on emergency room CT scans.
